function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and can include optional query parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

search.description: Query parameter to search for a specific term.

limit.description: Query parameter to limit the number of results.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers to include in the request as key-value pairs.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Authorization.description: Authorization credentials for connecting to the resource.

timeout.description: The amount of time to wait for a server response, in seconds. This is a float type value.

message.content: It looks like you’re referencing Apple’s revenue figure. Just to make sure I’m on the right track—are you asking about a specific year, quarter, or segment? For example, Apple’s total annual revenue in recent fiscal years has been in the $200 billion‑plus range (e.g., $365 billion in FY 2022). A $21 billion figure would be more typical for a single product line or a smaller company. Let me know which context you’re looking at, and I can pull up the exact numbers for you.
message.reasoning: The user says "Apple revenue was $21 billion." Likely they want to verify or get more info. We need to respond appropriately. Maybe ask for clarification or provide context. Could ask if they want more details about Apple's revenue, like year, source, etc. Or maybe they want to confirm. We can respond: "Which year?" Provide typical revenue numbers. Apple revenue $21B is low; Apple revenue is usually >200B. So maybe they refer to a specific segment? Might be a mistake. We can ask for clarification.
